fi-toim-vero-380530.s: The guide deals with VAT on the sale of scrap and scrap of metal, which has been subject to the reverse charge since 1 January 2015. The purpose of the introduction of the reverse charge is to reduce the loss of value added tax resulting from fraudulent activities and to improve the competitive situation of honest enterprises in the sector. The reverse charge is intended, inter alia, to prevent a procedure whereby the buyer deducts VAT which the seller fails to pay to the State.
fi-toim-vero-380530.t: Reverse VAT obligation on the sale of scrap and scrap metal

fi-tpa-100-2026.f: Initiative to launch national data centre strategy and overall impact assessment of data centre projects
fi-tpa-100-2026.s: The rapid increase in investment in the data centre challenges the capacity of the electricity system, the adequacy of energy generation, the investment needs of electricity networks and the ability of municipalities to assess the overall impact of projects, while ensuring national security of supply, overall security and the interests of taxpayers.
fi-tpa-100-2026.t: on the launch of the national data centre strategy and the overall impact assessment of data centre projects

fi-tpa-77-2026.f: Initiative for measures on the re-use of discarded batteries for repair
fi-tpa-77-2026.s: On 3 July, guidance published by the Finnish Agency for Authorisation and Control (LVV) on the handling and waste testing of spent batteries threatens to make the repair of electric and hybrid cars virtually impossible for independent car repair companies, and threatens to end the repair of batteries in Finland altogether.
fi-tpa-77-2026.t: Reuse of discarded batteries for repair

fi-tpa-78-2026.f: Initiative to ban the production, import and sale of halal- meat in Finland
fi-tpa-78-2026.s: The starting point of Finnish animal welfare legislation is that, in the case of slaughter, the animal is stunned before the bloodshed, so that it does not cause unnecessary pain and suffering, but this main rule has been exempted on religious grounds.
fi-tpa-78-2026.t: prohibiting the production, import and sale of halal meat in Finland

fi-tpa-79-2026.f: Initiative for measures to break down the deteriorating literacy process
fi-tpa-79-2026.s: The PISA results from 2025 describe the reduced skills of Finnish young people in literacy, mathematics and natural sciences. It is particularly worrying that the decline in literacy has continued throughout the 2000s. Finland is well known for a long time for its most equal school system in the world and for its excellent PISA results.
fi-tpa-79-2026.t: Measures to break down declining literacy trends

fi-tpa-80-2026.f: Initiative to reduce fuel prices by reducing the distribution obligation
fi-tpa-80-2026.s: Due to the significant increase in fuel prices, a reduction in the obligation to distribute fuels towards the EU minimum level is being undertaken.
fi-tpa-80-2026.t: Reducing fuel prices by reducing the obligation to distribute

fi-tpa-81-2026.f: Initiative for measures to protect minors against sexual events that are not appropriate for age
fi-tpa-81-2026.s: According to the Youth Act, ensuring the conditions for youth work is one of the tasks of the municipalities. Municipalities can organise their activities in the way they wish and using the partners. In some cases, this has led to activities that jeopardise children's and young people's right to safe development and to work at the age level. For example, the City of Helsinki organised the sewing work of the Packer and Packer bags on 25 June 2026.
fi-tpa-81-2026.t: on the protection of minors from sexual events that are not appropriate for age

fi-tpa-82-2026.f: Initiative to strengthen wild boar hunting to prevent the spread of African swine fever
fi-tpa-82-2026.s: African swine fever (ASF) is a serious threat to the Finnish pig economy, agriculture and forestry, domestic food production and security of supply. To prevent the spread of the disease, effective and proactive measures are needed, especially to reduce wild boar stock.
fi-tpa-82-2026.t: on stepping up the hunting of wild boar in order to prevent the spread of African swine fever

fi-tpa-83-2026.f: Initiative on intervention by the Russian Shadow fleet through a common European early warning system
fi-tpa-83-2026.s: The Russian Shadow Fleet constitutes one of the most acute security policy and environmental threats in the Baltic Sea. Russia is unscrupulously circumventing the sanctions imposed on the country's energy coasts, thus helping Russia to maintain its war economy, but also helping Russia to maintain the growth of the Shadow Fleet, the use of old and often unfit tanker equipment, and the unclear ownership and insurance regime.
fi-tpa-83-2026.t: on the intervention of the Russian Shadow fleet by a common European early warning system

fi-tpa-84-2026.f: Initiative to correct the calculation of the duration of the student credit without undermining the student's ability to obtain credit for the student's student's student's loan
fi-tpa-84-2026.s: In Finland, a defect has been identified in the regulation of student credit. In the current situation, a student who has performed military or civil service may lose the possibility of student credit for reasons beyond his control.
fi-tpa-84-2026.t: The Court of First Instance held that, in order to determine whether the amount of aid granted by the Member States to the applicant is compatible with the common market, it is necessary to examine whether the aid is compatible with the common market.

fi-tpa-85-2026.f: Initiative for voluntary conversion of development aid
fi-tpa-85-2026.s: Finland's public finances are in a serious situation, the debt of the central government is rising and public expenditure needs to be adjusted, and there are reasons for a critical assessment of secondary public expenditure.

fi-tpa-86-2026.f: Initiative to extend the employment benefit
fi-tpa-86-2026.s: Employee benefits, such as knowledge of lunch, culture and well-being, are an established part of Finnish working life, designed to support the well-being of employees, their working life, access to services, and the ability of employers to take care of their staff. In practice, benefits are offered through a wide range of service platforms such as Edenred, Smartum and Epassi.

fi-tpa-87-2026.f: Initiative to reduce electricity transmission charges
fi-tpa-87-2026.s: As the consumer cannot compete for the electricity transmission of the electricity network company in his region, the price of the network service does not result in normal market competition, which is why the affordability of electricity transmission pricing and effective regulatory oversight are of particular importance.
fi-tpa-87-2026.t: on the reduction of electricity transmission charges

fi-tpa-88-2026.f: Initiative on the impact of co-operation in the chain on competition
fi-tpa-88-2026.s: The Food Market Act was reformed during this government period, and it is now important to monitor that the law also works properly.
fi-tpa-88-2026.t: The effects of chain cooperation on competition

fi-tpa-89-2026.f: Initiative to launch a national quality register pilot for memory disorders
fi-tpa-89-2026.s: Mental diseases are one of Finland's most important growing public health and economic challenges. Finland has nearly 150 000 people with memory problems, and new diagnoses are made every year about 20 000, some of them working age. As the population ages, the number of people with illnesses continues to grow, which increases the need to develop prevention, diagnostics, treatment, rehabilitation and rehabilitation.
fi-tpa-89-2026.t: on the launch of a national register pilot for memory disorders

fi-tpa-90-2026.f: Initiative to provide for a mandatory disciplinary penalty for an ex-post session
fi-tpa-90-2026.s: According to the Basic Education Act, a student who interferes with the teaching or otherwise violates the order of the school or acts in a fraudulent manner may be ordered to sit for up to two hours.
fi-tpa-90-2026.t: on the introduction of a mandatory disciplinary penalty for the ex-post session

fi-tpa-91-2026.f: Initiative on speeding up the flow of information by public authorities on security-relevant authorisation issues
fi-tpa-91-2026.s: There have been serious shortcomings in the flow of information between authorities in situations where a person's right to conduct a profession subject to authorisation is affected by a conviction for a criminal offence.
fi-tpa-91-2026.t: on speeding up the flow of information by public authorities on security-relevant authorisation issues

fi-tpa-92-2026.f: Initiative to reduce the number of prison sentences and increase the maximum penalty
fi-tpa-92-2026.s: The Finnish penal system provides a discount for the perpetrators of more crimes. When multiple offences are dealt with at the same time, the penalty does not accumulate fully. This is called a large-scale discount.
fi-tpa-92-2026.t: on reducing the number of prison sentences and increasing the maximum penalty

fi-tpa-93-2026.f: Initiative to tighten the eligibility criteria of the Minister so that the Minister can only have Finnish citizenship
fi-tpa-93-2026.s: section 60 (1) of the Constitution states that the Council of State shall comprise a Prime Minister and a sufficient number of other ministers who must be Finnish citizens who are known to be honest and competent. The qualification of the Minister is therefore Finnish citizenship. However, the current regulation does not prevent a person acting as a minister from having, in addition to Finnish citizenship, one or more other States:
fi-tpa-93-2026.t: Strengthening the eligibility criteria of a minister so that the Minister can only have Finnish citizenship

fi-tpa-94-2026.f: Initiative to strengthen the employment of people with disabilities and persons with partial employment through a binding model
fi-tpa-94-2026.s: The employment gap between disabled and non-disabled persons is about 20.5 percentage points, which shows that current measures are not sufficient to ensure equal access to the labour market.
fi-tpa-94-2026.t: establishing the employment of disabled people and persons with partial employment through a binding model

fi-tpa-95-2026.f: Initiative on the return of the small group system corresponding to observation categories to basic education
fi-tpa-95-2026.s: The peaceful working conditions in schools, the safe learning environment for pupils and the right of every child to receive education in accordance with their individual needs require that, in basic education, adequate resources are available to meet the different learning, behaviour and school needs.
fi-tpa-95-2026.t: on the return of the small group system corresponding to the observation categories to basic education

fi-tpa-96-2026.f: Initiative for measures to safeguard alternative ways of dealing and to deliver service mail to people over 75, including by letter to prevent digitisation
fi-tpa-96-2026.s: Digital government and the digital skills needed in everyday life cause great difficulties for many older people. According to the old Commissioner, there are up to 500,000 to 600,000 people living in Finland who have no basic digital skills or lack the skills to do independent digital business.
fi-tpa-96-2026.t: on the protection of alternative forms of access and the delivery of service mail to persons over 75 years including by letter to prevent digitisation

fi-tpa-97-2026.f: Initiative on the introduction of pneumococcal vaccine in the national vaccination programme
fi-tpa-97-2026.s: The aim of the national vaccination programme is to protect Finns as well as possible against preventable diseases at the right time and at the lowest possible doses of vaccine. Vaccines included in the national vaccination programme are voluntary and free of charge. They are given at the clinic, school health care or at their own health centre.
fi-tpa-97-2026.t: on the administration of pneumococcal vaccine to a national vaccination programme

fi-tpa-98-2026.f: Initiative to limit the total amount of fees for non-parliamentary trust missions
fi-tpa-98-2026.s: At the same time, decisions can be taken at several levels of government in the context of trust measures in the municipality, welfare area or province. Therefore, the decision-making body can be at its best at four different levels of government.
fi-tpa-98-2026.t: on the limitation of the total amount of fees for trust missions other than those relating to parliamentary representation

fi-tpa-99-2026.f: Initiative to increase the penalties for rape offences, always condemning rape to unconditional imprisonment
fi-tpa-99-2026.s: The current legislation on minimum penalties for rape offences is far too lax: according to Section 1 of Chapter 20 of the Penal Code, rape is punishable by imprisonment for at least one and up to six years, and a maximum of two years' imprisonment can be imposed subject to general provisions. In practice, basic forms of rape can be sentenced to conditional imprisonment below two years.
fi-tpa-99-2026.t: on the punishment of rape offences, always condemning rape to unconditional imprisonment
